audit_name: Phase 2H-2 — Live Full-Room Deterministic Furniture Audit

kitchen_dining_area.label: Kitchen & Dining Area
kitchen_dining_area.impact: Room-grouping anomaly: combines architectural zones. All furniture instances are accurately captured in 3D with 0 position and rotation delta.

fallback_kitchen.label: Kitchen
fallback_kitchen.impact: Separated fallback room generated around kitchen-base counters; both kitchen-base instances are captured with exact 3D transforms.

empty_dining_area.label: Dining Area
empty_dining_area.impact: Contains no canonical furniture (only door opening). Does not cause missing furniture in 3D scene because the dining table is captured in kitchen-dining-area.

duplicate_bedroom_3_labels.description: duplicate Bedroom 3 labels with different room IDs
duplicate_bedroom_3_labels.impact: Distinct room IDs (bedroom-3 and bedroom-3-2) prevent ID collisions. bedroom-3 contains the main bedroom furniture (5 items), while bedroom-3-2 contains 1 window opening.

unresolved_limitations: Canonical 2D floor plans do not encode vertical 3D height, so height deltas are compared against procedural 3D specs rather than canonical values.
Three.js bounding boxes measure procedural multi-part mesh extents (pillows, handles, bevels) rather than raw planar bounding boxes.
Room-grouping anomalies (e.g. combined kitchen-dining-area and duplicate Bedroom 3 labels) remain in the source scene and are documented as read-only anomalies.
